paragraphs.text: Chapter 3 I HATE YOU GILBERT When school started in September, Ann and
Diana walked to school together.
Diana said to Ann, today you'll meet Gilbert Blythe.
He's very good looking.
Oh boys, said Ann.
I'm not interested in them.
But when Ann saw Gilbert in school, she did look at him closely.
He was tall with curly brown hair.
He had a friendly smile.
He is good looking.
Whispered Ann to Diana, the next day was quiet at the Avonlea school.
The teacher, Mr. Phillips, was in the back of the classroom.
He was helping some of the older children.
Ann was looking out the window.
She was dreaming.
Gilbert saw her and wanted to talk to her.
He whispered, Hey Ann!
Ann did not hear Gilbert.
She was imagining that she was flying in the wind above the beautiful trees.
Gilbert was surprised.
Usually girls wanted to talk to him.
He reached over and pulled Ann's hair.
Carrots!
Carrots!
He yelled.
Ann jumped up and looked at Gilbert.
What a horrible boy you are!
She shouted, I hate you.
Then she raised up her book and hit Gilbert's head.
Mr. Phillips saw Ann hit Gilbert with her book.
Ann said, Mr. Phillips.
Why did you do that?
Gilbert spoke up.
It was my fault, Mr. Phillips.
I was rude to her.
That's why she hit me.
Mr. Phillips was not happy with Ann.
That's no excuse to hit another student, he said.
Ann, go up and stand in front of the class.
Ann stood up in front of the class for the entire afternoon.
She looked very angry.
I hate Mr. Phillips, she thought.
And I hate Gilbert's life.
I'll never look at or speak to him again.
The next day, some of the boy students were playing in a field during lunch.
They were late for afternoon class.
Ann ran into the class with them, right behind Mr. Phillips.
Your late said Mr. Phillips.
You won't sit with Diana today.
I see that you enjoy being with the boys.
So you'll sit next to Gilbert this afternoon.
He can't be serious, she thought.
But Mr. Phillips was serious.
Did you hear me Ann?
He said, yes sir.
Ann said softly.
She picked up her books and moved slowly to the desk next to Gilbert.
Then she sat down and put her head on the desk.
I wasn't the only person who was late.
Thought Ann?
Why did Mr. Phillips make me sit with a boy?
And the worst boy is Gilbert Blife.
That afternoon seemed to last forever for Ann.
When school was over and went back to her desk,
she picked up all her books, pens and pencils.
What are you doing?
I'm not coming back to school.
Said Ann.
Oh no!
But Ann, we're going to read a new book.
And we'll play a game on Monday.
It'll be very exciting.
But Ann didn't care.
That evening, Marilla visited Mrs. Lind.
Rachel, please give me some advice.
Ann says she's not going back to school.
What should I say to her?
Of course, Mrs. Lind already knew all about Ann's troubles at school.
Well, Marilla, said Mrs. Lind.
I've raised ten children myself.
So I can tell you, don't worry.
Leave Ann alone.
She'll want to go back to school soon.
So Marilla did nothing.
And Ann stayed at home.
One day, Marilla found Ann crying in the kitchen.
What's the matter, child?
Ask Marilla in surprise.
I miss Diana very much.
So, Dan, I can't live without her, Marilla.
But what will happen when she gets married?
I hate her husband already.
I can imagine her in church with her white dress.
She'll leave me then, and I'll never see her again.
Marilla tried not to laugh, but she couldn't help it.
She laughed and laughed.
Ann raised her head and stared at Marilla.
Suddenly, she felt very foolish.
The next day Ann went back to school.
All the children were very happy to see her again, especially Diana.
However, Ann did not speak to Gilbert Bly.
She was still mad at him, and she thought she would never forgive him.
